title: Aucubin directly targets beta-catenin to co-suppress Wnt and HIF-1 pathways in ovarian cancer: Computational and experimental validation.
authors: Pan, Zhijian; Wu, Han; Liu, Yancai; Yu, Haoyang; Shu, Jiayi; Yang, Changyan; Wang, Jianglong; Du, Fengxia; Shao, Min; Zhou, Hefeng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Aucubin靶向β-catenin抑制卵巢癌Wnt/HIF通路，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: OV is a highly lethal malignancy plagued by chemoresistance, necessitating the development of novel therapeutic agents. The Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, driven by its central component beta-catenin (CTNNB1), is a key oncogenic axis in OV, making it an attractive therapeutic target. We employed an integrated strategy combining in vitro assays (MTT, Western blot), in silico analyses (network pharmacology, WGCNA, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations), and biophysical validation assays (CETSA, DARTS) to systematically investigate the anti-cancer mechanism of the natural compound AU. AU potently inhibited the viability of A2780 OV cells by inducing apoptosis. Our comprehensive bioinformatic analysis identified CTNNB1 as a high-confidence direct target of AU. Clinical data confirmed that CTNNB1 is overexpressed in OV and correlates with poor patient prognosis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations predicted a stable AU-CTNNB1 interaction, which was then experimentally validated by both CETSA and DARTS, confirming direct target engagement in a cellular context. Mechanistically, AU treatment resulted in the dose-dependent suppression of key proteins in the Wnt/beta-catenin and HIF-1 signaling pathways. AU exerts its anti-OV activity by directly binding to CTNNB1. This interaction inhibits the oncogenic Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, leading to the concurrent suppression of the HIF-1 pathway and the induction of apoptosis. Our study provides a complete mechanistic rationale for the development of AU as a novel targeted therapy for ovarian cancer.
abstract_zh: OV是一种高度恶性的恶性肿瘤，受化疗耐药性困扰，亟需开发新型治疗药物。Wnt/β-catenin通路由其核心组分β-catenin（CTNNB1）驱动，是OV中的关键致癌轴，使其成为有吸引力的治疗靶点。我们采用了一种整合策略，结合体外实验（MTT、Western blot）、计算机模拟分析（网络药理学、WGCNA、分子对接、分子动力学模拟）以及生物物理验证实验（CETSA、DARTS），系统研究了天然化合物AU的抗癌机制。AU通过诱导凋亡有效抑制了A2780 OV细胞的活力。我们的综合生物信息学分析将CTNNB1鉴定为AU的高置信度直接靶点。临床数据证实，CTNNB1在OV中过表达，并与患者不良预后相关。分子对接和动力学模拟预测了稳定的AU-CTNNB1相互作用，随后通过CETSA和DARTS实验验证，确认了在细胞环境中的直接靶点结合。机制上，AU处理导致Wnt/β-catenin和HIF-1信号通路中关键蛋白的剂量依赖性抑制。AU通过直接结合CTNNB1发挥其抗OV活性。这种相互作用抑制了致癌的Wnt/β-catenin通路，导致HIF-1通路的同步抑制和凋亡的诱导。我们的研究为AU作为卵巢癌新型靶向治疗的开发提供了完整的机制依据。
